## Grading Summary

**Answer-key coverage:** All 12 key items are captured; figures, owners and dates are correct throughout, including both in-meeting corrections ($395,000 → $358,000; October 30 → October 13; Friday the 18th → Friday the 25th for the worksheet).

**Not-actions:** Clean. The maiden-name question appears only as a life-event note recording the deferral (item 16), not as an action; the declined term policy on Gavin and the declined $40,000 cash distribution are absent from the action lists entirely.

**Extras:** Mostly well-supported background (settlement terms, mortgage math, support, college, insurance, Social Security). Two items double-count work already recorded elsewhere: item 23 restates the beneficiary change already logged as action item 29, and item 30 splits out the "release on entry of judgment" condition already written into account action 19.

key_items.note: Signing date Sept 10, 2026 and hearing Oct 13, 2026 both match; correctly uses the corrected hearing date rather than the erroneous Oct 30.
Effective Oct 1, 2026 with $118,000 to $127,500; added 8% deferral plus match is also accurate.
$358,000 and 48.93% are the corrected figures; in-kind pro rata and release on entry of judgment captured. Account opening is logged separately at item 17.
$212,400 as of June 30 plus or minus gains and losses, full direct rollover with nothing withheld and no cash out, into the new rollover IRA.
$45,000 sold from bills to Fallowbrook savings; the $53,800 share and ~$8,800 residual both match the transcript.
Graciela, Thursday Sept 17, 2026; no figures involved.
Uses the renegotiated Friday Sept 25 deadline, not the initial Friday the 18th; scope (house alone, half of Lucia's college) matches.
Graciela obtains the Fallowbrook loan estimate by end of October 2026; correctly drops the adviser's abandoned plan to line up lenders.
Noor, Friday Sept 18, 2026; all four components plus the custodian-routed signature page for Gavin are present.
Graciela, day of entry Oct 13, 2026, correctly gated on entry of judgment. Item 23 restates the same change as an account action.
Silas, Monday Sept 21, 2026; $212,400 correct and all three review points (June 30 valuation, loan exclusion, separate alternate-payee account) captured.
Silas, for the Nov 10, 2026 meeting; age 65, Moderate, support ending 2033 and the Social Security comparison all included.

extra_items.note: Home retention, 12-month refinance obligation and every figure ($301,000 balance, $2,246/$1,456 at 3.125% from 2021, ~$1,878 P&I and ~$2,668 all-in at 6.375%) match the transcript.
Settlement division of the joint brokerage as a life event; uses the corrected $358,000 with $731,600 account value, 48.93% and Gavin's $373,600.
QDRO award terms as a life event; $212,400 as of June 30, Gavin's ~$424,000 balance and the ~$18,000 original plan loan all stated in the meeting.
She keeps her entire 403(b) per the settlement.
$2,850/month for seven years from Nov 1, 2026 through Oct 2033, non-taxable to her and non-deductible to Gavin under post-2019 rules.
$1,410/month until Mateo graduates, expected June 2028.
Gavin's 529 with ~$11,000 used first, then 50/50; ~$18,000/year after scholarship, her ~$9,000/year or ~$750/month starting next fall.
W-4 changed in June; adviser confirmed head of household is right given entry by Dec 31 and Mateo living with her.
$500,000 term with her as irrevocable beneficiary until support ends; carrier letter received last week and held by Joanna.
Children stay on Gavin's plan until they age out; she is on her hospital plan.
Will and health care proxy done by Joanna's office in June.
24-year marriage, FRA 67, own record versus divorced-spouse benefit whichever is higher.
~$6,900/month now rising to ~$7,300 post-refinance; ~$12,000/month income matches the adviser's 'a little under twelve thousand'.
Correctly logged as a life-event note that the maiden-name change was considered and deferred, not as an action.
Opening the new individual taxable account titled Graciela M. Kettridge is a distinct agreed step from the journal itself.
Noor confirmed the rollover IRA is opened now, empty, so the account number is ready for Quillmoor's instructions.
Risk tolerance moved from Growth to Moderate applying to everything the firm manages; the allocation/IPS update is distinct from sending the signature packet.
Restates the beneficiary change already recorded as action item 29; same accounts, same 50/50 split with sister as custodian, same gating on entry of judgment.
Splits out the release condition already written into account action 19 (release once Joanna confirms entry, within 30 days); adds no new commitment.
